hints: Look closely at the polymer backbone, it still contains C=C double bonds, so this cannot be a normal saturated addition polymer.
Split the section into repeating blocks and you will see the repeat unit is $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-$ with four carbons and one double bond.
Think about which small alkene could open up to give that 4-carbon unit while still leaving one double bond behind in the chain.
walkthrough:
**Notice what is unusual**

Most addition polymers you meet are fully saturated, with only single bonds in the backbone. Here the chain still has $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds, so the monomer must have had more than one double bond to start with.

Polymer section:
$$-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-$$

**Find the repeat unit**

Divide the section into identical blocks. Each block is four carbons long.

Repeat unit:
$$-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2]-$$

**Work back to the diene monomer**

A conjugated diene like buta-1,3-diene can add in a 1,4-way. One $\pi$-bond breaks to join to neighbours, the other $\pi$-bond shifts to the middle of the new unit.

1,4-addition:
$$n\,\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow -[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2]_n-$$
That matches the given section exactly, so the monomer is buta-1,3-diene.

options.A: Ethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$, gives poly(ethene) with repeat unit $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2]-$. This is fully saturated with no $\text{C}=\text{C}$ in the chain and only 2 carbons per repeat, so it cannot match.
options.B: Propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$, gives poly(propene) with repeat unit $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)]-$. This has a methyl side chain and no double bonds in the backbone, so it does not fit.
options.C: But-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$, would give a saturated unit $-[\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)]-$. Again there would be no $\text{C}=\text{C}$ left in the polymer and there would be methyl branches, which are not seen.
options.D: Buta-1,3-diene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$, undergoes 1,4-addition polymerisation. The two outer carbons form new single bonds to neighbours, leaving a central double bond to give $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2]-$, exactly the section shown.
